source.display_title: 05/09/2026 - Kamal Mohammed & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

call.sequence_note: Direct follow-up to the 2026-05-08 call with the same rep, booked at the end of it. Opens mid-thread with 'I've been doing my research yesterday. I've got a couple of questions for you.' Fields marked as established on the prior call are noted as such; nothing is carried over silently.

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Not referenced on this call; setter code taken from the title and corroborated by the prior call in this sequence ('You spoke with Kim, didn't you').

prospect.name: Kamal Mohammed
prospect.location: Chicago, Illinois, USA; originally from Sheffield, UK — established on the prior call
prospect.occupation: Convenience store owner — established on the prior call
prospect.family_status: Married; wife away visiting family and returning the day after this call
prospect.training_background: Essentially untrained; owns no equipment — 'I don't have no equipment or nothing'. Full history established on the prior call.
prospect.medical: Nothing disclosed on this call. Poor posture and self-described bad back were disclosed on the prior call and remain unscreened.

signals: Consistent with the prior call's assignment; nothing on this call changes it
The decade of unkept intent resurfaced as the rep's main lever: 'you've been saying for like 10 years that you're going to get shredded'
New signal — genuine doubt that transformation is possible for him at all: 'I believe it, and I don't... I feel like, is it even possible?'
Counter-signal remains that he has never trained systematically, placing him closer to a first-timer than a classic rebuilder

goals.text: Transform his body and get shredded, carried over as the stated objective throughout

pains.text: Genuine doubt that transformation is achievable for him — 'I believe it, and I don't'
Cannot see enough transformation evidence to believe the programme works
Liquidity friction — needs to move money into the bank and clear credit cards before paying
Wife has reacted negatively to the price

objections.raw_quote: I've been seeing his programs and stuff. It says $200 a month memberships. What's the difference between what you're saying and what I'm seeing?
objections.rep_response: Distinguished the products cleanly and did not offer the cheaper one as an alternative — 'that's not the coaching... it's basically just self-guided stuff. Like it's just resources. There's no plan there. There's no nutrition plan.' The prospect accepted the distinction himself: 'that's way like too low.'

objections.raw_quote: if I was to say like $1,200, $1,000 to $6,000, $7,000, that's still a difference within the six months, you know, where I'm coming from... Because at the end of the day, it's all, it's still money at the same time, you know, like, no one's got free money to give away
objections.rep_response: Reframed the price as the mechanism of the result — 'the reason why it's $1,000 a month is even more reason why you should do it... because you've been saying for like 10 years that you're going to get shredded... you are going to get shredded because you put the money in' — plus a best-of-the-best quality claim.

objections.raw_quote: How come like, you know, like when I try to look up his results, he don't really have so much results. only got like three, four, five people. Like we don't really have like a community of people, like where I can see like a lot of results and transformations
objections.rep_response: Claimed 'We've coached over 1,200 people' and screen-shared client interviews. The prospect was not satisfied by what he was shown and repeated the objection.

objections.raw_quote: It is, like, I'll be honest, like, I believe it, and I don't. I don't believe it, I feel like, I don't know, I mean like, as in like, I believe like, I can transform my body and at the same time, I feel like, is it even possible? I don't even know, like, well, is it possible?
objections.rep_response: Named it correctly — 'It sounds like there's a little bit of certainty missing' — then answered with assertion rather than the scripted reframes: 'Yeah, 100% it's possible', 'It's a little bit of fear, dude, and it's normal. It's supposed to be a little bit scary.'

objections.raw_quote: Would you do a thousand monthly?
objections.rep_response: Declined outright and held the price: 'literally can't do anything on numbers. It'd have to be 12.' Then re-presented the existing structures rather than inventing a new discount.

objections.raw_quote: I'm gonna wait till my wife comes tomorrow, I'm gonna see what she thinks too.
objections.rep_response: Asked one probing question — 'What do you think she thinks?' — received a deflection, and then dropped the subject entirely. The wife's prior reaction had already been reported as hostile to the price and was never addressed.

objections.raw_quote: No, listen, this is the last time we're going to set up one more meeting, yeah? ... Do us a meeting for Monday, and I'll process the meeting on Monday.
objections.rep_response: Pressed the hesitation three separate times — 'What's holding you back from doing it now?', 'It doesn't sound like the money's the problem, brother. Sounds like there's something else holding you back', and 'otherwise you'd just do it now if you were 100%' — plus a do-the-dishes analogy and a $1,200-now bridge. The prospect denied any blocker each time and held the deferral.

tiers.terms: two payments of $3,000; second payment window stated inconsistently as 30-60 days, then 90 days, then end of month
$1,200 per month for six months — 'an extra $1,200 total'
per month, self-guided Skool community; explicitly identified as not the coaching

offer.payment_plan_terms: Full ladder stated explicitly for the first time in this sequence: $6,000 upfront, or 2 x $3,000, or $1,200 monthly totalling $7,200. The rep recommended against the monthly route — 'if you do it in six, you're paying an extra grand for no reason' — and refused to negotiate below it. He then improvised a fourth structure: '$1,200 down, we get you all started... and then if you wanted to do 3, then you can just pay the other 1800... you've got until the end of the month to do the other 1800, to keep it at the 6'. That $1,200 plus $1,800 constitutes the first $3,000 tranche of the two-payment plan, with a further $3,000 to follow.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent; the rep confirmed payment would be processed together on a call
Third scheduled contact booked — Monday at 4pm — with a new Zoom invite sent and confirmed as received after landing in spam
Prospect committed verbally and emphatically many times: 'I'm 100% doing it. I already made my mind up', 'Don't even think about a million percent'
Counter-evidence: this is now the second consecutive deferral in the sequence, having promised on 2026-05-08 to message the next day and pay after visiting the bank
Counter-evidence: two unresolved objections remain live — insufficient transformation proof, and a wife who has already called the price crazy and had not yet been consulted
Counter-evidence: the rep pressed the hesitation three times and could not surface a blocker the prospect would name, which usually indicates an unstated one
No onboarding call with Trevor was booked; only a further sales call
outcome.next_step: Payment call Monday at 4pm, at which the prospect intends to pay either $1,200 or $3,000 by credit card after clearing balances and consulting his wife.

notable.note: The clearest statement of the price ladder anywhere in this batch, and it confirms a $7,200 monthly variant that sits outside the approved structure. The second-payment deadline was stated three different ways in twenty minutes — 30 to 60 days, then 90 days, then end of month. The rep also used the identical '$1,200 down plus $1,800 keeps it at the 6' construction that appears on the Brian Muthami call the same day; here the remaining $3,000 is implied by context, and on that call it was never mentioned at all. Positively, the rep refused an explicit request to discount to $1,000 a month and held the price, and correctly declined to offer the $200/month community as an alternative to coaching — the opposite of what happened on the Varun Shankar call the previous day.

quality.notes: Severe. The opening exchange is fully inverted — the prospect's question about $200 memberships and the rep's answer both sit under the prospect's label. The price ladder at 00:01:07 to 00:01:21 alternates labels mid-explanation, putting '$1,200 a month' under the rep and 'So it would be an extra $1,200 total' under the prospect when the reverse is true. The long block from 00:14:47 to 00:16:06 merges both speakers with no reliable separation at all. Role was read from content throughout.
